stage: A -- protocol lock, written before the pilot submission
purpose: Reproduce ProcessBench's OWN published critic-model evaluation category (general LLM prompted to critique a solution step by step) on our OWN strongest model, over the SAME 3,400 ProcessBench rows already teacher-forced for the GL-LIU study. This completes item 4 ('critic-model ceiling') of the reasoning-localization benchmark's ordered wishlist (docs/research_notes/reasoning_localization_methods_and_benchmarks_2026.md) -- not a new dataset, a new competing column on identical inputs.

mandatory_competitor_gate.paper: ProcessBench: Identifying Process Errors in Mathematical Reasoning -- Zheng et al., arXiv:2412.06559
mandatory_competitor_gate.official_code: github.com/QwenLM/ProcessBench, code/run_eval.py + code/templates/critique_template.txt (fetched verbatim 2026-08-10, hash-worthy quotes in spectral_utils/processbench.py's CRITIC_TEMPLATE docstring)
mandatory_competitor_gate.dataset_subset: same Qwen/ProcessBench rows (gsm8k, math, olympiadbench, omnimath) already used by pb_llama31_8b_external_v1.json and the original 8 Qwen3-4B/8B cells
mandatory_competitor_gate.protocol: single user-turn prompt (no system message), paragraphs tagged <paragraph_i>...</paragraph_i>, greedy decoding (temperature=0), \boxed{} index extraction, exact-match F1 = harmonic mean of error-row accuracy and correct-row accuracy
mandatory_competitor_gate.supervision_access_sampling: zero-shot prompted critique, no training, one extra large-model generation per row (NOT gray-box -- this is the 'critic model' access category in docs/research_notes/reasoning_localization_methods_and_benchmarks_2026.md, distinct from our own single-pass gray-box DUFS-LIU)
mandatory_competitor_gate.comparison_level: 1 for the dataset (identical rows/labels to every other ProcessBench cell in this project); the critique text itself is new model output, exactly as ProcessBench's own protocol requires -- there is no 'same outputs' notion for a critic baseline

model.selection_rationale: "prioritize jobs applicable for benchmarking" (Omri, 2026-08-10) -- our strongest model gives the critic-model ceiling its best shot, same rationale as the HLE preset's model choice earlier this session.
model.attn_impl: sdpa -- eager's O(T^2) fp32 attention-score materialization OOM'd this exact model on long single-sequence generation during the HLE pilot this same session (job 169914/170046); this driver needs no attention capture, so sdpa is the safe default from the start, not a reactive fix.

prompt.paragraph_tagging:
<paragraph_{i}>
{step}
</paragraph_{i}>

, joined and .strip()'d -- exact code from prepare_input_boxed
prompt.chat_turn: single user message, no system prompt (matches messages=[{'role':'user','content':prompt}])

decoding.note: run_eval.py's own default for every non-QwQ model (QwQ gets 32768; not applicable to Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct). Fixed identically between pilot and full run per project convention -- never varied to save pilot cost.

grading.extraction: extract_critic_prediction -- last \boxed{...} match, int-parsed, None on failure or non-integer payload (matches run_eval.py's extract_answer exactly, including the bare except->None)
grading.match_rule: exact index equality against ProcessBench's own `label` field (0-indexed paragraph, or -1 for 'all correct') -- NOT tolerance-one, matching run_eval.py's `pred == d['label']`
grading.metric: critic_f1() in spectral_utils/processbench.py -- error_acc (match rate on label != -1 rows), correct_acc (match rate on label == -1 rows), F1 = harmonic mean of the two, verbatim from run_eval.py's own acc1/acc2/f1 computation

pilot_plan.seed_note: load_processbench's own seeded rng(0) draw -- same 30-row pilot population used by every other ProcessBench pilot in this project (see spectral_utils/processbench.py's own comment on why a random, not head, draw is required for class balance)
pilot_plan.health_gate: both classes present per subset (label==-1 and label!=-1), no systematic \boxed{} parse failure (n_unparsed should be a small minority, not the majority -- a large n_unparsed means the model isn't following the requested output format and the whole cell would be uninformative), no wholesale truncation (n_truncated should be ~0 given max_new_tokens=8192 is generous for a short critique)
pilot_plan.no_full_run_yet: the full N=3400 run is NOT submitted in this pass -- report pilot health back before scaling, per this project's own local-smoke -> N=30-pilot -> full-N gate order (CLAUDE.md).

cost_estimate.basis: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct single-sequence generation throughput observed on this same cluster during the HLE full run (2026-08-09/10): ~19-25s/problem at up to ~2048 tokens for HLE's longer explanations; ProcessBench critiques are expected to be considerably shorter on average (reviewing a handful of paragraphs then one \boxed{} line, not an open-ended explanation) despite the higher 8192-token cap, so per-row cost should track actual critique length, not the cap.
cost_estimate.pilot_120_rows: expected well under 1 hour on a single B200 given the above

still_out_of_scope: the full N=3400 run (separate approval after pilot health review)
voting/self-consistency mode (run_eval.py's --use_voting; not attempted here -- single greedy generation only, matching every other cell's decoding policy)
QwQ-32B or o1-mini as an additional critic model (ProcessBench's own strongest critics; would be a second, separate job)
